## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

d1_cs <- tibble(
  group = rep(c("A", "B", "C"), c(38, 42, 40))) %>%
  mutate(category = c(
    rep(c("X1", "X2", "X3", "X4"), c(10, 10, 9, 9)),
    rep(c("X1", "X2", "X3", "X4"), c(12, 10, 11, 9)),
    rep(c("X1", "X2", "X3", "X4"), c(12, 9, 10, 9))
  ))

```

```{r}
break_assoc <- function(data, variable_to_shuffle){
  data %>% 
    mutate(shuffled = sample({{variable_to_shuffle}}, replace = FALSE))
}

chi_sq <- function(data, group, category, count){
  data %>%
    group_by({{group}}) %>%
    mutate(row_total = sum({{count}})) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    ## Now the column total
    group_by({{category}}) %>%
    mutate(column_total = sum({{count}})) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    # now the grand total
    mutate(grand_total = sum({{count}}),
           expected = row_total * column_total / grand_total,
           resid = ({{count}} - expected) / sqrt(expected))
}

d_counted <- d1_cs %>% count(group,category) 

%>% 
  chi_sq(group, category, n)

resid_null <- map(1:1000, \(i) {
  d1_cs %>% 
    break_assoc(category) %>%
    count(group,shuffled) %>% 
    chi_sq(group, shuffled, n) %>%
   max(resid))
}) %>% list_rbind()

# visualisation - 
# 176
```
